text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- The Association of Saving Banks see no danger of a strong rise in interest rates in the next few years.
- The Statistics Office's barometer for business cycles shows that industry leaders have a positive view of the propects for the third quarter.
- Norway's state-owned energy company Statoil reported operating profits in the first half of 1997 up 23 percent at 10.1 billion crowns primarily because of higher oil prices.
- Shipping company Leif Hoegh reported a 50.5 percent increase in operating profits for the first half of 1997 to 289 million crowns against 192 million in the 1996 period.

- Kvaerner will not accept Belship's offer to buy Kvaerner's stake in Western Bulk Shipping for 38 crowns per share. Kvaerner says its shares in Western Bulk are worth 18 percent more than the 93 million crowns Belships has offered.

- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) expects about one billion crowns in profit in the first half of 1997. Peter Forsman, head of information, says the numbers for the second quarter are so positive that SAS will achieve the same result as for the first half of 1996. Since the first quarter shares in SAS on the Oslo bourse have climbed 71 percent.
